name: Structured interview with scored rubric
what: Every candidate is asked the same predetermined job-related questions in the same order, and every answer is scored on the same rating scale with behavioural anchors [41](#cite:41). It is the most valid single predictor in the 2022 re-estimation (.42) and carries a smaller [Black–White difference](#term:subgroup-difference) (.23) than tests of knowledge (.54) or [cognitive ability](#term:cognitive-ability-test) (.79) [1](#cite:1).

evidence.effect: operational validity .42 (Sackett et al. 2022), the highest of any single predictor [1](#cite:1); structured .44 vs unstructured .33 in McDaniel et al. 1994 [5](#cite:5)
evidence.population: structured-interview databases k = 36 / N = 3,069 (McDaniel) and k = 69 / N = 4,795 (Huffcutt et al. 2014) as pooled in [1](#cite:1)

what_it_does_not_do: Its validity varies widely between studies, so a poorly built one is not the .42 interview [52](#cite:52) [3](#cite:3). Its group difference is not negligible: corrected for first-screen [range restriction](#term:range-restriction), two behavioural interviews showed d of .36 and .56 [18](#cite:18). It does not measure what a [work sample](#term:work-sample-test) measures, and it does not survive interviewers who were not trained in it [19](#cite:19).
costs: Question development and a rubric per competency, interviewer training and calibration; Google reports that prepared questions and rubrics then save about 40 minutes per interview, as the company states it [42](#cite:42).
how_to: Define the competencies from the job, then write behavioural (past experience) and situational (hypothetical) questions for each [41](#cite:41).
Write a rating scale with anchors for poor, borderline, solid and outstanding answers, and have interviewers record answers in full [42](#cite:42).
Ask the same questions in the same order of every candidate and score with the same scale [41](#cite:41).
Train and calibrate interviewers; training is the antecedent that predicts use of the valid components [19](#cite:19) [42](#cite:42).

name: Combine the evidence by formula, not by feel
what: Each predictor is scored, the scores are weighted and added, and the total is the anchor for the decision. The same information combined by formula predicts job performance at r .44 against .28 when combined by judgement [7](#cite:7); managers who override a valid test make worse hires on average [10](#cite:10).

evidence.effect: mechanical r .44 (cross-validated .40) vs clinical r .28 for job performance [7](#cite:7); override hires worse than test-concordant hires [10](#cite:10)
evidence.population: k = 9 job-performance comparisons, N ≈ 1,392 / 1,156 [7](#cite:7); 15 service-sector firms [10](#cite:10)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not collect the information; experts remain good at that [7](#cite:7). It does not remove the need to validate what is scored (c-unvalidated-criteria), and a formula built on a weak proxy such as years of experience (.07) is a precise way of being wrong [1](#cite:1).
costs: A scoring sheet per stage and the discipline to document any deviation from the anchor score [7](#cite:7).
how_to: Use [mechanical methods](#term:mechanical-combination) to screen; use the mechanical score as the anchor for any adjustment [7](#cite:7).
Document deviations from the anchor and the reason [7](#cite:7).
Average ratings across multiple raters [7](#cite:7).

name: Work sample or job-knowledge test built from the job
what: Have candidates do a sample of the actual work, or test the knowledge the job requires, scored against a standard. [Job knowledge tests](#term:job-knowledge-test) predict at .40 and [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) at .33 [1](#cite:1); applicants rate work samples second only to interviews for fairness [14](#cite:14). A standardised test added to informal screening at a national retailer raised median tenure by more than 10 percent without reducing minority hiring [11](#cite:11).

evidence.effect: job knowledge .40 (k = 59, N = 3,965); work samples .33 (k = 54, N = 10,469) [1](#cite:1)
evidence.population: pooled civilian samples [1](#cite:1); a 1,363-store retail natural experiment [11](#cite:11)

what_it_does_not_do: Both carry large [group differences](#term:subgroup-difference) (knowledge d .54; work samples d .67) [1](#cite:1), so they are better used for pass/fail prerequisites than for ranking, which the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) treat as needing more validity evidence [32](#cite:32). A work sample tests skills the person already has, not what training will give them, and building one is technically demanding enough that the evidence summaries advise expert help [17](#cite:17).
costs: [Job analysis](#term:job-analysis), test construction, standardised administration and scoring, and expert review [17](#cite:17).
how_to: Derive the sample from a job analysis; standardise administration and scoring [17](#cite:17).
For jobs with substantial training, test the prerequisites that will not be trained [17](#cite:17).
Keep the exercise representative of the work rather than a puzzle the role never poses (the relevance complaint in [22](#cite:22)).

name: Technical assessment in private or collaborative format
what: Replace the watched whiteboard with a private focus session followed by retrospective think-aloud, or with collaborative problem-solving. In a [randomised trial](#term:field-experiment), candidates solving the same problem unobserved performed more than twice as well with lower measured stress [21](#cite:21); developers themselves ask for collaborative formats [22](#cite:22).

evidence.effect: performance reduced by more than half when watched; stress and cognitive load higher in the traditional format [21](#cite:21)

what_it_does_not_do: One small trial with students, so the [effect size](#term:effect-size) in working engineers is unknown; the format change does not supply validity on its own, which still depends on the exercise being a sample of the job [1](#cite:1) [17](#cite:17).
costs: A quiet room and a retrospective interview protocol; little else ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Let the candidate work privately, then walk through their reasoning afterwards (retrospective think-aloud) [21](#cite:21).
Or run the exercise as a collaborative problem-solving session with the team [22](#cite:22).

name: Realistic job preview
what: Candidates hear the hard parts of the job and the firm before they decide: the hours, the site, the customer, the [clearance](#term:security-clearance) wait, the pay range. Across 40 studies previews lowered inflated expectations and reduced attrition during recruiting and voluntary turnover [12](#cite:12); across 52 studies the effect ran mainly through perceived organisational honesty rather than through self-selection [13](#cite:13).

evidence.effect: lower initial expectations, lower attrition during recruitment, lower voluntary and total turnover, higher performance [12](#cite:12); organisational honesty the primary mechanism [13](#cite:13)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not fill a pipeline; some candidates leave because of it, which is the point [12](#cite:12). The [effect sizes](#term:effect-size) were not read in this sweep (todo), so the magnitude is not quoted. It cannot make an unattractive offer attractive ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: Candour early in the process, which may shrink the pipeline before it saves a hire (synthesis from [12](#cite:12)).
how_to: Match the preview to the outcome targeted: timing and medium moderate the effect [12](#cite:12).
Oral or written previews that signal honesty, delivered at or after hiring, were most effective for retention [13](#cite:13).

name: Decide fast and extend the offer fast
what: Reserve interview windows, set a response-time target, and pre-approve the offer range so the offer can follow the final interview within days. Earlier post-interview offers were more often accepted in both student and experienced pools at one large company, with no later performance or turnover penalty [15](#cite:15).

evidence.effect: earlier offers more likely accepted; no performance or turnover difference by offer speed [15](#cite:15)
evidence.population: N = 3,012 archival records at one company [15](#cite:15)

what_it_does_not_do: One company's archival data [15](#cite:15); the acceptance [effect sizes](#term:effect-size) were not read (todo). Speed does not substitute for an affordable range [98](#cite:98) or for a process applicants find fair [16](#cite:16); a fast offer below the market is still declined ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: Manager calendar discipline and a pre-authorised [pay band](#term:pay-range-posting-law) (synthesis).
how_to: Speed post-interview offers to raise acceptance and shorten vacancies without hurting performance or turnover [15](#cite:15).

name: Interview plan and process preview
what: Assign competencies to interviews so no two interviewers cover the same ground, and tell candidates at first contact how many steps there are and how long they take. Procedural-justice perceptions and face validity predict attraction and acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14); withdrawal tracks perceptions of the process and differs by stage [16](#cite:16).

evidence.effect: applicant perceptions correlate with organisational attractiveness, acceptance and recommendation intentions (average r .08–.52) [14](#cite:14)

what_it_does_not_do: Fewer interviews raise the stakes of each question; the validity comes from content and structure, not from brevity [5](#cite:5) [1](#cite:1) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). No primary study of the number of rounds against withdrawal was found.
costs: A written interview plan per opening (synthesis).
how_to: Define the attributes to assess and assign each to an interview with its own questions and rubric [42](#cite:42).
Explain the process and timeline at first contact (synthesis; the perception mechanism is [14](#cite:14)).

name: Interviewer training and calibration
what: Everyone who interviews is trained in the structured method and calibrates their ratings against the others'. Formal training was the modifiable antecedent of using the structure components that carry validity among 131 professional interviewers [19](#cite:19).

evidence.effect: training and a selection focus predicted question sophistication, consistency, note-taking and standardised evaluation [19](#cite:19)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not remove rapport-building and probing, which interviewers resist giving up [19](#cite:19); it is a condition for the [structured interview](#term:structured-interview)'s validity, not a source of validity on its own ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: [Training time](#term:flsa-training-time) for every interviewer and periodic calibration sessions [42](#cite:42).
how_to: Train interviewers on the questions, the rubric and note-taking; calibrate ratings in groups [42](#cite:42).

name: Validate the screen and keep the records
what: Each criterion, test and question is tied to a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis); criterion-related, content or construct validity evidence is kept; selection rates are recorded by sex and by race or ethnic group; and the documentation the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) describe is kept [31](#cite:31) [32](#cite:32). For an [automated screen](#term:algorithmic-screening), the anti-bias testing and the ADS records that California now treats as a defence factor and a four-year retention duty are kept as well [40](#cite:40).

evidence.effect: binding framework under Title VII; professional standard in the SIOP Principles [29](#cite:29)
evidence.population: employers covered by Title VII; federal contractors additionally

what_it_does_not_do: Documentation does not make a weak predictor strong, and the [four-fifths rule](#term:four-fifths-rule) is a rule of thumb that courts have declined to treat as conclusive [35](#cite:35). The bottom-line rule means a firm with no overall [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact) is generally not expected to validate each component [31](#cite:31).
costs: A job analysis per role family, a selection-rate log, and expert help for anything beyond content validation ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [29](#cite:29) [17](#cite:17)).
how_to: Choose criterion-related, content or construct validity evidence tied to important elements of job performance [32](#cite:32).
Keep selection-rate records by sex and by race or ethnic group; sampling is allowed at high volume [31](#cite:31).
Where ranking is used, hold more validity evidence than pass/fail use requires if ranking has more adverse impact [32](#cite:32).
For vendor tests, obtain the validation documentation; the employer remains responsible [33](#cite:33).

name: Monitor selection rates by group
what: Compute each group's selection rate at each stage and compare to the highest group's; a rate below [four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) is generally regarded as evidence of [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact), qualified by statistical and practical significance and by small numbers [31](#cite:31). Self-analysis of this kind is what the EEOC's withdrawn 2023 technical assistance recommended for [algorithmic tools](#term:algorithmic-screening), and what California's regulations reward [35](#cite:35) [40](#cite:40).

evidence.effect: the Uniform Guidelines' four-fifths rule of thumb [31](#cite:31)

what_it_does_not_do: It detects impact; it does not justify the procedure, which still needs job-relatedness [33](#cite:33). With small applicant pools the rule is unreliable and the Guidelines say agencies may look at longer periods or similar uses elsewhere [31](#cite:31).
costs: A stage-by-stage log of applicants and outcomes by group, collected with the safeguards the Guidelines describe [31](#cite:31).
how_to: Record selection rates by sex and by race or ethnic group; evaluate components when the overall process shows impact [31](#cite:31).
Ask vendors whether their tool was tested for substantially lower selection rates and by what standard [35](#cite:35).

name: Replace negative filters with affirmative skill criteria
what: Configure the applicant-tracking screen to search for the skills and experience the [core requirements](#term:essential-requirement) need rather than to reject anyone missing a degree, a title or an unbroken history, as the Harvard Business School and Accenture report recommends [44](#cite:44). The discarded proxies are weak: years of experience .07 [1](#cite:1).

evidence.effect: 88% of employers reported exact-match rejections of qualified high-skilled candidates [44](#cite:44); experience-years validity .07 [1](#cite:1)
evidence.population: HBS/Accenture employer survey (sizes not in the article) [44](#cite:44)

what_it_does_not_do: It widens the pool without assessing it; the validity has to come from what follows (l-work-sample-or-knowledge-test, l-structured-interview) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Degree-requirement removals announced by large firms produced little actual change in who was hired, which is the skills-based-hiring controversy (sweep 2) [58](#cite:58).
costs: Reconfiguring the ATS and writing skill criteria from a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) (synthesis).
how_to: Change filters from negative (screen out) to affirmative (search for the skills and experience core requirements need) [44](#cite:44).

name: Pareto-optimal predictor weighting
what: Weight the predictors to trade a little validity for a large reduction in [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact), using the Pareto-optimal decision aids reviewed in the diversity-validity literature [25](#cite:25).

evidence.effect: judged among the three most promising strategies; evidence described as thinner for criterion weighting [25](#cite:25)

what_it_does_not_do: It needs validity data the small firm usually lacks, and the review's own summary is that no strategy resolves the dilemma [25](#cite:25). Banding reduces adverse impact mainly when minority preference is applied within bands, which raises its own legal questions [25](#cite:25).
costs: Local validity data and statistical help ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Use compensatory predictor composites and Pareto-optimal weighting across stages [25](#cite:25).

name: Sequence the inquiries around the conditional offer
what: Every inquiry the law reserves sits on the far side of a conditional offer, and the posting is written for the people the law actually allows. Before the offer: ability to perform job functions with or without accommodation, licences, attendance, and (for non-contract roles) arrest or conviction records [34](#cite:34). After the offer: medical questions and examinations asked of everyone in the job category [34](#cite:34); criminal history for positions under a federal contract, with exceptions for classified-access and national-security positions [48](#cite:48); and individualised assessment where a record is disqualifying [47](#cite:47). For export-controlled work, the posting states that [U.S. persons](#term:us-person) include nationals, permanent residents, refugees and asylees, and export screening stays out of the [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) [51](#cite:51) [49](#cite:49).

evidence.effect: ADA, Title VII guidance, the Fair Chance Act and 8 U.S.C. 1324b as enforced [34](#cite:34) [47](#cite:47) [48](#cite:48) [49](#cite:49) [50](#cite:50)
evidence.population: all employers; federal contractors; ITAR/EAR employers

what_it_does_not_do: It does not change what may ultimately be required (a [clearance](#term:security-clearance), a [drug test](#term:drug-free-workplace), a U.S.-person status); it fixes when and how it is asked. Cleared positions are largely exempt from the [Fair Chance Act](#term:fair-chance-act)'s timing rule [48](#cite:48).
costs: A rewritten application form and posting template, and a two-stage checklist ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Pre-offer: ask whether the applicant can perform job functions with or without reasonable accommodation [34](#cite:34).
Post-offer: medical inquiries only if required of all entering employees in the same job category [34](#cite:34).
Build a targeted criminal-record screen on the nature of the offence, time elapsed and the job, with individualised assessment [47](#cite:47).
Do not say export rules require a citizenship; keep export assessments separate from Form I-9 [51](#cite:51).

name: Employee referral program with a bonus tied to tenure
what: Employees are asked to refer people from their networks and receive a bonus when the [referral](#term:referral-hiring) is hired and again when they pass a tenure milestone. Referred hires quit 10 to 30 percent less across nine firms in three industries and were worth about 25 percent more in discounted profit in the one firm where it could be computed [60](#cite:60); in a financial-services firm referred applicants were 7.3 points more likely to be interviewed, 2.4 points more likely to be offered, and about 15 percent less likely to leave [61](#cite:61).

evidence.effect: quit rates 10–30% lower; profit per worker \$2,201 vs \$1,756 (trucking); hire probability higher [60](#cite:60) [61](#cite:61)
evidence.population: nine firms, three industries, hundreds of thousands of applicants [60](#cite:60); one firm, 62,127 applications [61](#cite:61)

what_it_does_not_do: Referred workers are not more productive on ordinary metrics; the value is in retention and rare events [60](#cite:60). Referrals from below-median workers were worth less than non-referred hires [60](#cite:60). Networks are segregated, so a referral-fed firm reproduces its founders' composition until cumulative hiring dilutes it [81](#cite:81); the selection-rate records the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) expect will show the effect [31](#cite:31).
costs: The bonus and the administration; the trucking firm's model assumed \$500 per referral plus \$500 at 26 weeks for experienced drivers, as inferred from its profit formula [60](#cite:60).
how_to: Weight the program toward above-median performers' referrals, whose referrals were worth four times those of below-median referrers [60](#cite:60).
Pay part of the bonus at a tenure milestone, as the studied firm did at 26 weeks [60](#cite:60).
Track referral hires by group against the [four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) test [31](#cite:31).

name: Track qualified rate, starts and retention by source
what: The source of every applicant is recorded and the cohort is followed to qualified, interviewed, offered, started and retained at 90 days and one year. Inside sources show higher tenure and performance than outside ones [62](#cite:62); the difference is invisible without the record ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Contractors kept online search and [applicant records](#term:applicant-record-retention) under the [Internet Applicant rule](#term:executive-order-11246) until its removal with part 60-1 on October 26, 2026 [87](#cite:87) [86](#cite:86); the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines)' selection-rate records by group remain [31](#cite:31).

evidence.effect: source effects on turnover and performance are meta-analytic (Zottoli & Wanous 2000, via [62](#cite:62)); the tracking practice itself is guidance

what_it_does_not_do: Small samples mislead: one good hire from a board is not a channel effect (synthesis from [62](#cite:62)). Recording source does not improve any channel by itself; the inside-source advantage is a tenure and performance difference measured across sources [62](#cite:62), and no study of the record-keeping practice itself was found.
costs: A source field in the applicant record and a quarterly tally (synthesis).
how_to: Keep selection-rate records by sex and by race or ethnic group at each stage; add source as a field [31](#cite:31).
Compare sources on starts and 90-day retention, not applicant volume (synthesis from [62](#cite:62)).

name: Rewrite the posting: searchable title, pay range, plain requirements, neutral wording
what: The posting uses the title candidates search for, shows the pay range, states the real requirements and the hard [constraints](#term:constraint-record) (site, schedule, [clearance](#term:security-clearance)), and carries no gendered or age-coded words. Within a job title, a 10 percent higher posted wage draws 7.7 percent more applicants [65](#cite:65); 59 percent of US postings and 63 percent of software-development postings already show pay [75](#cite:75); [masculine-coded wording](#term:gendered-wording) lowers women's appeal and belonging for the same job [77](#cite:77); "recent college graduate" and "young" are unlawful age terms [78](#cite:78); a citizenship restriction on export-controlled work is unlawful unless law or contract requires it [49](#cite:49).

evidence.effect: +10% posted wage → +7.7% applicants within title [65](#cite:65); wording effect on appeal 4.16 vs 4.50 [77](#cite:77)
evidence.population: CareerBuilder postings [65](#cite:65); 493 and 3,640 ads plus three experiments [77](#cite:77)

what_it_does_not_do: A better posting does not raise the pay or lift the onsite requirement; candour about them thins the pipeline, which is the realistic-job-preview trade-off [12](#cite:12). Thirteen states and the District of Columbia require a range in the posting, so the range is a duty before it is a [lever](#term:lever-record) [76](#cite:76).
costs: Writing time; a pay range the firm can defend (sweep 3) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Title: the market's name for the job, since titles carry most of the applicant-count signal [65](#cite:65).
Pay: show the range; required in thirteen states and DC [76](#cite:76) and present in most competing postings [75](#cite:75).
Wording: remove masculine-coded terms [77](#cite:77) and the listed age terms [78](#cite:78); write "[U.S. person](#term:us-person)" where export rules apply, never "citizen only" [51](#cite:51).
List the opening with the state workforce agency if [VEVRAA](#term:vevraa) applies [73](#cite:73).

name: Offer remote or hybrid work where the contract allows
what: The posting is opened to candidates who will not relocate by making the work remote or hybrid. Workers assign a hybrid option a mean value of 8 percent of pay, and 239 of 470 surveyed firms expanded or plan to expand remote work to keep staff and moderate wage growth [70](#cite:70); 28 percent of paid workdays were at home in mid-2023 [69](#cite:69); 1.6 percent of job seekers relocated for a job in early 2023 [85](#cite:85).

evidence.effect: WFH valued at 8% of pay (mean); half of firms use it in place of wage growth [70](#cite:70)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not exist for classified or site-bound work, and a customer's access rules decide, not the firm [119](#cite:119) (sweep 4). The 8 percent valuation is a mean over workers who differ widely [70](#cite:70), and the option does nothing for a role the customer requires onsite.
costs: Where allowed, little; where not, the 8 percent differential the firm competes against [70](#cite:70).
how_to: State the real arrangement in the posting; candidates price it [70](#cite:70) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

name: Replace credential requirements with skill requirements where the job allows
what: The degree or years-of-experience line comes off the posting when the [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) does not support it, and the skills are named instead. Years of experience predicts performance at .07 [1](#cite:1); the non-degree hires made after requirement removals stayed longer [68](#cite:68); nearly 70 percent of campus-recruiting employers report using [skills-based hiring](#term:skills-based-hiring) [79](#cite:79).

evidence.effect: announced removals produced a 3.5-point rise in non-degree hiring in affected roles and less than one hire in 700 economy-wide; retention of non-degree hires higher [68](#cite:68)

what_it_does_not_do: Changing the posting without changing the screen produced almost no change in who was hired [68](#cite:68); the [lever](#term:lever-record) works only with l-affirmative-skill-filters and an assessment that carries the validity [1](#cite:1) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Where a contract [labor category](#term:labor-category) requires a degree, the requirement is the customer's (sweep 7).
costs: A job analysis per role family and a rewritten screen (synthesis).
how_to: Derive requirements from a job analysis; keep only criteria tied to important elements of job performance [32](#cite:32).
Change the ATS filter to search for the named skills [44](#cite:44).

name: Military transition pipeline (SkillBridge, fellowships, VEVRAA listing)
what: Host transitioning service members in their last 180 days under a [SkillBridge MOU](#term:skillbridge), or through a twelve-week corporate fellowship, and list openings with the state workforce agency where [VEVRAA](#term:vevraa) applies. A small employer commits to at least one participant a year and to a 75 percent qualifying-offer rate on completion [74](#cite:74); the fellowships run twelve weeks [83](#cite:83); 8.3 million veterans are in the labour force at 3.5 percent unemployment, and 41.8 percent of employed Gulf War-era II men work in management, professional and related occupations [72](#cite:72); VEVRAA listing brings priority [referral](#term:referral-hiring) of protected veterans [73](#cite:73).

evidence.effect: program terms [74](#cite:74) and the listing duty [73](#cite:73); pool size [72](#cite:72)
evidence.population: transitioning service members; 8.3 million veterans in the labour force [72](#cite:72)

what_it_does_not_do: No study of SkillBridge hiring outcomes was found; the 75 percent figure is an obligation, not a result [74](#cite:74). Whether fellows hold [clearances](#term:security-clearance) is not in these sources, so the pipeline's value for cleared roles is unestablished (todo).
costs: A liaison, a training plan, incident and outcome reporting at 90 and 180 days [74](#cite:74); no wage cost during the internship per the law-firm summary [59](#cite:59).
how_to: Sign the SkillBridge MOU; commit to the minimum intake for the firm's size and the 75% offer standard [74](#cite:74).
List every opening with the state workforce agency job bank, concurrently with other recruiting [73](#cite:73).

name: University and early-career pipeline
what: Recruit from campuses through career-services platforms and internships. Employers expect to hire 5.6 percent more Class of 2026 graduates and look first for teamwork, problem-solving and communication on entry-level résumés [79](#cite:79). The posting must avoid the listed age terms, including "recent college graduate" [78](#cite:78).

evidence.effect: planned +5.6% hiring of the Class of 2026 [79](#cite:79)

what_it_does_not_do: Early-career hires need the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity), [mentoring](#term:mentoring) and placement the develop stage covers (sweep 5), and a customer may not accept junior personnel on a [labor category](#term:labor-category) (sweep 7).
costs: Platform fees as the vendors state them (sweep 8); supervisory time ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Write the posting around skills and attributes, not graduation year [78](#cite:78) [79](#cite:79).

name: Manage the employer image candidates actually see
what: The firm's work, people and terms are put where candidates look, and whoever recruits is trained. Favourable [employer images](#term:employer-image) relate to better recruitment outcomes and form through recruiters and word of mouth [64](#cite:64); recruiter behaviour, process perceptions and job and organisation characteristics predict attraction, and recruiter demographics do not [63](#cite:63); perceived fit is the strongest predictor [62](#cite:62).

evidence.effect: category-level predictors of attraction and job choice, mediated by attitudes and intentions [63](#cite:63)

what_it_does_not_do: Image does not offset a material pay gap or an unattractive job; the job and organisation characteristics are the predictors [63](#cite:63) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Specific content tactics (employee testimonials, examples of work) are untested as such.
costs: Recruiter training and content the firm is allowed to publish; customer approval for examples of program work (synthesis).
how_to: Train recruiters on personableness, competence, trustworthiness and informativeness, the recruiter attributes that predict attraction [62](#cite:62).
Describe the work and the organisation accurately; fit perceptions predict most [62](#cite:62) [63](#cite:63).

name: Audit who the ad actually reaches
what: The audience a paid ad platform delivered is checked against the occupation's workforce. A gender-neutral STEM ad reached fewer women because the algorithm optimised cost and young women are an expensive audience [66](#cite:66). California treats targeted job advertisements as an [automated-decision system](#term:automated-employment-decision-tool) [40](#cite:40), and selection-rate records by group are expected under the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) [31](#cite:31).

evidence.effect: skewed delivery of a neutral ad through cost optimisation [66](#cite:66)

what_it_does_not_do: Platforms may not expose delivery demographics; the audit then has to be run on the applicant pool instead ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: Platform reporting and a comparison against occupational data (synthesis).
how_to: Ask the platform for delivery demographics; compare applicant demographics to the occupation (synthesis from [66](#cite:66) [31](#cite:31)).

name: Set the range from the labor-category rate and the market, before recruiting
what: The range is worked backwards from the contract: the [labor category](#term:labor-category)'s hourly rate contains wages, [overhead](#term:overhead-rate), [G&A](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) and profit [98](#cite:98), so the affordable salary is the rate less the firm's indirect rates and margin ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The result is then checked against the market: [OEWS](#term:oews) wages for the occupation and metro area [110](#cite:110), the [ECI](#term:employment-cost-index)'s 3.1 percent annual wage growth [103](#cite:103), awarded ceiling rates for comparable categories in CALC+ [111](#cite:111), and for [cleared](#term:security-clearance) work the premium ladder [89](#cite:89). A pre-approved range lets the offer follow the final interview within days [15](#cite:15).

evidence.effect: the rate ceiling is contractual [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); speed of offer raises acceptance with no later penalty [15](#cite:15)
evidence.population: T&M and labor-hour contractors; one firm's offer-timing data (N = 3,012) [15](#cite:15)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not raise the rate; where the arithmetic yields a range below the market, the choice is rate relief, a different labor category, a different work model or a narrower pool (synthesis). Under cost-type contracts the range must also be reasonable by comparison with similar firms and sit inside an established plan [100](#cite:100).
costs: A one-page [wrap-rate](#term:wrap-rate) calculation per labor category and a quarterly market check (synthesis).
how_to: Take the category rate from the contract [98](#cite:98); subtract fringe, overhead, G&A and [fee](#term:fee) at the firm's own rates (synthesis).
Compare with the OEWS metro estimate for the SOC code [110](#cite:110) and the CALC+ ceiling for the same education and clearance [111](#cite:111).
Pre-authorise the range so the offer is not delayed by approval [15](#cite:15).

name: Post the range and say whether pay is negotiable
what: The range goes in the posting, with a plain statement of whether it is negotiable. State [posting laws](#term:pay-range-posting-law) raised disclosure by about thirty points and wages by 1.3 to 3.6 percent with no loss of employment or postings [97](#cite:97); most competing postings already show pay [75](#cite:75); within a title, a higher posted wage draws more applicants [65](#cite:65). Saying pay is negotiable removed the gender gap in who negotiates in a [field experiment](#term:field-experiment) with nearly 2,500 applicants [95](#cite:95).

evidence.effect: negotiation gap closes or reverses when negotiability is stated [95](#cite:95); posting laws +1.3–3.6% wages, +30 pp disclosure [97](#cite:97)
evidence.population: ≈ 2,500 job seekers [95](#cite:95); US state adopters, three datasets [97](#cite:97)

what_it_does_not_do: Posting a range the firm cannot pay does not help; a range invites comparison by incumbents (c-new-hire-pay-compresses-incumbents) and coworker transparency lowers average wages by about 2 percent in the bargaining model [90](#cite:90). Negotiated differences must still rest on job-related factors [112](#cite:112).
costs: None beyond candour; thirteen states and DC require the range anyway [76](#cite:76).
how_to: Show a good-faith range in every posting [76](#cite:76) [97](#cite:97).
State explicitly whether pay is negotiable [95](#cite:95).

name: Review incumbents before the offer and budget the adjustments
what: Before extending an offer, compare it with what incumbents in substantially equal jobs earn and decide what their adjustments will cost. External hires came in about 18 percent above internal promotees and performed worse for two years [93](#cite:93); below-median earners who learn peers' pay become less satisfied and search more [92](#cite:92); a gap must be cured upward [112](#cite:112) and prior pay is no defence in the Ninth Circuit [116](#cite:116).

evidence.effect: external premium ≈ 18% with worse performance and higher exit [93](#cite:93); asymmetric satisfaction and search response to peer pay [92](#cite:92)
evidence.population: one investment bank, 2003–2009 [93](#cite:93); UC employees, randomised information [92](#cite:92)

what_it_does_not_do: It makes the retention cost visible; it does not pay it. Raising incumbents is a recurring cost that may need a rate conversation with the customer (c-contract-rates-lag-market) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Where the job is not substantially equal, the [Equal Pay Act](#term:equal-pay-act) does not require parity, but Title VII still reaches pay [112](#cite:112).
costs: A comparison per offer and the adjustments it reveals, which Bidwell''s figure suggests can be large [93](#cite:93).
how_to: Compare the offer with incumbents in substantially equal jobs by content, not title [112](#cite:112).
Budget the adjustments or document the job-related factor that justifies the difference [112](#cite:112).
Consider the internal route: promotees cost less and perform better for two years [93](#cite:93).

name: Put the whole package and the arrangement in the offer
what: State benefits and arrangements in dollars and terms candidates can compare. Benefits are 30 percent of private-industry compensation cost [104](#cite:104); a family health premium is about \$27,000 with the employer paying roughly three quarters [105](#cite:105); workers value a work-from-home option at about 8 percent of wages and predictable schedules at about 20 percent [115](#cite:115); working conditions are a central part of compensation [94](#cite:94).

evidence.effect: amenity valuations ≈ 8% (WFH) and ≈ 20% (schedule predictability) of wages [115](#cite:115); benefits 30% of cost [104](#cite:104)
evidence.population: call-centre applicants, discrete-choice experiment [115](#cite:115); BLS ECEC [104](#cite:104)

what_it_does_not_do: Noncash value does not offset a material base-pay gap [63](#cite:63) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); a firm that offers no health coverage, as 41 percent of small firms do not, has nothing to state on that line [105](#cite:105). [Cleared](#term:security-clearance) and onsite work cannot offer the arrangement premium (sweep 4).
costs: A statement template and the firm''s own benefit costs (synthesis).
how_to: List employer-paid premium, retirement contribution and paid leave in dollars (synthesis from [104](#cite:104) [105](#cite:105)).
State the arrangement (remote, hybrid, schedule predictability) as a term, since candidates price it [115](#cite:115).

name: Request a rate adjustment with market and recruiting evidence
what: The firm uses the contract's price-adjustment mechanism, or the next option or [recompete](#term:recompete), to move the labor rate, and brings the evidence: [ECI](#term:employment-cost-index) wage growth of 3.1 percent [103](#cite:103), CALC+ ceiling rates for the same category, education and [clearance](#term:security-clearance) [111](#cite:111), and its own declined offers and departures ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). On GSA schedules the clause allows up to three increases a period inside a window, thirty days apart, with approval beyond ten percent; GSA suspended those limits in 2022 when inflation ran ahead of them [117](#cite:117).

evidence.effect: the adjustment mechanism and its limits [117](#cite:117); the market series [103](#cite:103)
evidence.population: GSA MAS contractors; T&M contractors generally

what_it_does_not_do: Relief is discretionary, bounded and slow; it rarely arrives for the vacancy in hand (synthesis). Wage-determination floors move on the Department of Labor's schedule, not the firm's [101](#cite:101).
costs: A written request with evidence; the customer''s time (synthesis).
how_to: Request inside the clause's window; stay within the approval threshold or document the case beyond it [117](#cite:117).
Attach the ECI series and CALC+ comparables [103](#cite:103) [111](#cite:111).

name: Sign-on and retention bonuses under a written plan
what: If the firm uses bonuses, write the plan first. Under cost-type contracts a bonus is [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) only when paid under an agreement made before the services or a consistently followed plan, and major plan changes need the administrative contracting officer's chance to review [100](#cite:100). Four in five organisations use [sign-on bonuses](#term:signing-bonus) and two in three [retention bonuses](#term:retention-bonus); one in eight evaluates whether they work [118](#cite:118).

evidence.effect: prevalence only; no effectiveness evidence found [118](#cite:118)

what_it_does_not_do: No study of sign-on or retention bonus effectiveness was found in this sweep; the [lever](#term:lever-record) is common practice, not evidence. An ad hoc bonus promised in an offer letter is unallowable on a cost-type contract [100](#cite:100). A visible sign-on bonus is a relative-pay signal to incumbents [92](#cite:92) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: The bonus; the plan document; the ACO review for plan changes [100](#cite:100).
how_to: Adopt the plan before the offer; keep it consistent across hires [100](#cite:100).
Measure whether it changed acceptance or retention; most firms do not [118](#cite:118).

name: Contingent offers to proposed key personnel, with disclosure
what: When a candidate is named in a proposal, write the contingency into the offer, keep the candidate engaged through award, and know the disclosure rule. At GAO an offeror with actual knowledge that a key person has become unavailable must notify the agency, and the proposal becomes unacceptable unless discussions reopen [108](#cite:108); declarations of continued availability have defeated dismissal motions [114](#cite:114). The Court of Federal Claims requires only a reasonable belief at submission unless the solicitation says more [109](#cite:109).

evidence.effect: GAO notification rule [108](#cite:108); COFC good-faith standard [109](#cite:109)
evidence.population: federal competitions with named key personnel

what_it_does_not_do: It does not shorten the government's award timeline or guarantee the candidate waits; the candidate-side bridge (paid [interim](#term:temporary-eligibility) work, milestones) is a clear-and-start [lever](#term:lever-record) (sweep 4). The two forums disagree, so counsel and the solicitation text decide the firm''s duty [108](#cite:108) [109](#cite:109).
costs: Contact and candour during a wait the firm does not control; possibly [bridge pay](#term:bridge-work) (sweep 4) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Read the solicitation for an express notice requirement [109](#cite:109).
Keep a current letter of commitment or declaration from each named person [114](#cite:114).
Notify the agency promptly if a named person becomes unavailable [108](#cite:108).

name: Do not ask for prior pay; set the offer from the job
what: Remove prior- and current-pay questions from applications, interviews and offer calls, and set the offer from the range for the job. Roughly twenty states and several localities bar the question, some bar confirming until an offer is out [106](#cite:106); the early bans raised the gender earnings ratio by about 1 percent, mainly among job changers [96](#cite:96); in the Ninth Circuit prior pay cannot justify a pay difference at all [116](#cite:116).

evidence.effect: gender earnings ratio +1% in ban states [96](#cite:96)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not tell the firm what to pay; the range has to come from the rate and the market (l-set-range-from-rate-and-market). A candidate may volunteer prior pay, and some states then permit confirmation [106](#cite:106).
costs: None ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Strike the question from every form and script [106](#cite:106).
Anchor on the posted range, not on what the candidate used to earn [116](#cite:116) [97](#cite:97).

name: Confirm the sponsorship path before the requisition is posted
what: Before the opening is advertised, establish with the facility security officer which of three paths the hire will take: [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) of a current eligibility, a [temporary eligibility](#term:temporary-eligibility) pending investigation, or a full investigation; and confirm the contract need that justifies a request at all. A request needs access essential to a classified contract and may cover only the minimum number of employees [119](#cite:119); a pre-award [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) needs the solicitation, written contracting-officer authorization and a pre-award DD 254 [146](#cite:146); a pre-employment investigation needs a written commitment and a start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119). The answer decides whether the posting may say "must obtain" and what start date it can promise.

evidence.effect: the need rule, the 45-day start rule and the sponsorship documents [119](#cite:119) [146](#cite:146)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not create a need where there is none, shorten the investigation, or guarantee a temporary eligibility, which is withheld whenever adverse information appears [119](#cite:119). Without a [facility clearance](#term:facility-clearance) there is no path at all [120](#cite:120).
costs: Security-officer time before recruiting starts; a later posting where the need is not yet documented ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Identify the contract or solicitation and the DD 254 that requires the access [146](#cite:146).
Decide reciprocity, temporary or full investigation from the candidate's current eligibility [119](#cite:119) [122](#cite:122).
If the investigation precedes employment, obtain the written commitment and plan a start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119).

name: Get the facility clearance sponsored before cleared hiring can begin
what: An uncleared firm cannot apply for its own [entity eligibility determination](#term:facility-clearance); a government contracting activity or a [cleared](#term:security-clearance) contractor [sponsors](#term:clearance-sponsorship) it when the firm needs access to compete or perform [120](#cite:120) [146](#cite:146). The package goes through NISS; the senior management official, the facility security officer and the insider-threat official must be cleared; foreign ownership, control or influence must be mitigated; the key officials' [questionnaires](#term:sf-86) and fingerprints are due by day 45 [146](#cite:146) [120](#cite:120). The government funds the processing [146](#cite:146), and an [interim](#term:temporary-eligibility) determination is at the agency's sole discretion [120](#cite:120).

evidence.effect: the sponsorship rule, the key-official requirement and the 45-day package clock [120](#cite:120) [146](#cite:146)

what_it_does_not_do: It carries no stated [end-to-end](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) timeline; the key officials'' clearances take the same investigation clock as any other [146](#cite:146) [126](#cite:126). A firm whose determination is invalidated cannot bid on new classified work [120](#cite:120).
costs: A sponsor's willingness to carry the firm; the key officials' time and disclosure; FOCI mitigation where ownership requires it [120](#cite:120) [146](#cite:146).
how_to: Secure a sponsor with a bona fide need: a GCA for a [prime](#term:prime-contractor) requirement or a cleared prime for a [subcontract](#term:subcontractor) [146](#cite:146).
Complete the NISS package within the first twenty days; submit the key officials' e-QIPs and fingerprints by day 45 [146](#cite:146).
Resolve FOCI and the record-of-integrity requirements before the vetting [120](#cite:120).

name: Run already-eligible and sponsored hiring as separate tracks with separate dates
what: Split [requisitions](#term:requisition) by the clock they sit on. A candidate with current eligibility of equal or higher level transfers by [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity), which the rule sets at five business days [122](#cite:122); a [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) candidate waits on an industry investigation that averaged 197 days for a [Secret](#term:secret) and 243 for a [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) in FY2026 Q3 [126](#cite:126). Planning the two tracks apart lets the firm fill an urgent opening from the first and grow the pool from the second without promising a start the second cannot meet ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

evidence.effect: reciprocity 5 business days [122](#cite:122) against 197–243 days end to end [126](#cite:126)

what_it_does_not_do: The five-day standard is not met reliably and is not tracked [145](#cite:145); the sponsored track still needs a contract need before anyone can be submitted [119](#cite:119). Neither track shortens adjudication, now the longest phase [126](#cite:126).
costs: Two pipelines to run; recruiting spend on a developmental track whose hires arrive months later (synthesis).
how_to: Tag each requisition "must hold" or "may obtain" and attach the current [DCSA](#term:dcsa) [end-to-end](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) figure to the second [126](#cite:126).
For "must hold" openings, ask for the level, the investigation date and any exception that blocks reciprocity [122](#cite:122).
Set the developmental track's start dates from the clearance clock, not from the vacancy date [126](#cite:126) [119](#cite:119).

name: Request temporary eligibility where nothing adverse has surfaced
what: The cognizant security agency may grant [temporary eligibility](#term:temporary-eligibility) for Confidential, [Secret](#term:secret) or [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) only if no adverse information is found; it may not exceed one year without approval; a temporary Secret is valid at that level but not for RD, COMSEC or NATO information until the final grant; [SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information) and SAP access on a temporary basis is the granting authority's separate decision; a non-U.S. citizen is ineligible; and withdrawal is not a denial and cannot be appealed [119](#cite:119). The policy comes from SEAD 8 of May 2020 [121](#cite:121).

evidence.effect: the conditions and limits of temporary eligibility [119](#cite:119) [121](#cite:121)

what_it_does_not_do: No public figure says how often contractor applicants receive it or how long the decision takes [127](#cite:127). It does not reach the categories of information many defence programs need, and a customer may decline to accept it ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: A start that can be withdrawn without appeal; access limited to the interim level [119](#cite:119).
how_to: Submit the [questionnaire](#term:sf-86) and fingerprints as early as the commitment allows [119](#cite:119) [146](#cite:146).
Confirm with the customer that an interim is acceptable for the work and for the facility [119](#cite:119) (synthesis).
Keep the hire off RD, COMSEC, NATO, SCI and SAP material until the final grant [119](#cite:119).

name: Recruit for a transferable eligibility and check the exceptions before the offer
what: Agencies must accept an investigation and adjudication of equal or higher level unless an exception applies: new adjudicatively relevant information, an investigation older than seven years, an adjudication recorded with an exception, a [Bond Amendment disqualifier](#term:bond-amendment) for [SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information), SAP or RD, an agency requirement the Security Executive Agent approved, an [interim](#term:temporary-eligibility) or limited grant, or a current denial or revocation [122](#cite:122). A [polygraph](#term:polygraph) cannot be a reason to withhold [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity); it is scheduled after the preliminary determination [122](#cite:122). Access can be restored after a break in employment without a new investigation where eligibility continued [119](#cite:119).

evidence.effect: the reciprocity rule and its seven exceptions; five business days [122](#cite:122)

what_it_does_not_do: The record often is not where the receiving agency can see it: 28 of 31 agencies told GAO their systems at times lacked the information, and the data on how long transfers take is unreliable [145](#cite:145). An interim held elsewhere does not transfer [122](#cite:122), nor does an interim credential [137](#cite:137).
costs: A narrower pool: the already-cleared contractor population was about 1.35 million on the last count [80](#cite:80); a premium in [cleared](#term:security-clearance) pay [89](#cite:89).
how_to: Ask for level, investigation date and whether the grant was final, before the offer [122](#cite:122).
Check the seven-year rule and any recorded exception against the position's requirement [122](#cite:122).
Submit the reciprocity request on acceptance and escalate at five business days [122](#cite:122) [145](#cite:145).

name: Shorten the interval and keep contact through it
what: Shorten the time between acceptance and the first day, and where the [clearance](#term:security-clearance) or the award sets that time, manage the wait: a named contact, a pre-start check-in, a first-day plan, regular contact when the start slips, and a realistic preview of the work [144](#cite:144). Each additional week raised the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by 22 percent among 157,154 accepted offers; good company communication roughly halved them (OR 0.56), a [referral](#term:referral-hiring) more than halved them (OR 0.42) [144](#cite:144).

evidence.effect: offer-to-start week OR 1.22; communication quality OR 0.56; referral OR 0.42 [144](#cite:144)
evidence.population: entry-level offers at one telecommunications employer (N = 157,154); survey of 434 adults [144](#cite:144)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not shorten a clearance or move an award date; the population studied is entry-level and customer-facing, so the rates do not transfer to cleared technical hires, only the direction [144](#cite:144). A competing offer (OR 1.18) still wins some of the time [144](#cite:144).
costs: Recruiter and manager time during a wait that produces no billable work [148](#cite:148) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Set the earliest start the compliance clocks allow and move the paperwork ahead of the start [144](#cite:144) [130](#cite:130).
Name one contact; schedule a check-in before the start; send a first-day plan [144](#cite:144).
When the start slips, say so at once and say what happens next [144](#cite:144).

name: Identify funded work for the wait before hiring ahead of the clearance
what: Before a [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) hire is made, decide what the hire will do and who pays while the [clearance](#term:security-clearance) runs. Contract hours are paid only for qualified labor performed on the contract [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); other payroll is an [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) allocated through the firm's pools and rates [148](#cite:148). Whether unclassified contract work is open to an uncleared hire depends on the contract's security terms [146](#cite:146) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); internal projects, proposal work and training are the firm's to fund (synthesis). The hire cannot be sponsored ahead of a contract need to shorten the wait [119](#cite:119).

evidence.effect: the cost rules that decide who pays for the wait [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148)
evidence.population: NISP contractors on T&M, labor-hour and cost-type work

what_it_does_not_do: No study of [bridge-work](#term:bridge-work) practice or of its effect on whether hires stay through the wait was found; the only evidence on the wait itself is that financial security lowers the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) (OR 0.86) and a competing offer raises them [144](#cite:144). The cost sits in the firm's rates and narrows what it can pay elsewhere (synthesis from [148](#cite:148)).
costs: Unbillable payroll for the length of the [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness), 197 to 243 days on the current figures [126](#cite:126); a budget line in the indirect rates [148](#cite:148).
how_to: Read the contract's security terms for what an uncleared employee may do on it [146](#cite:146) (synthesis).
Budget the interval in the indirect rates before the offer, not after the start slips [148](#cite:148).
Tell the candidate what the bridge work is and how long it is funded [144](#cite:144).

name: Run the access steps with named owners before the start date
what: A list of every access the first productive day needs, and who grants each: the credential [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) through TASS with the fingerprint check and the submitted investigation [138](#cite:138) [137](#cite:137); the [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) request with its five-day standard [122](#cite:122); the [SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information) or SAP read-in and any [polygraph](#term:polygraph) [119](#cite:119) [122](#cite:122) [147](#cite:147); the cyber qualification the role needs on day one [139](#cite:139); the customer's own [onboarding](#term:onboarding) interval, 41 days from a favourable determination at DHS in FY2026 Q3 [125](#cite:125). A named contact and a first-day plan are among the practices the one field study on [no-shows](#term:new-hire-no-show) recommends [144](#cite:144).

evidence.effect: the access prerequisites and their owners [137](#cite:137) [138](#cite:138) [139](#cite:139) [122](#cite:122)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not give the firm authority over any of the owners; the customer's security office and the sponsoring official act on their own clocks [138](#cite:138) [145](#cite:145). No study of checklists in this setting was found.
costs: Security-officer and manager time; a start date set later than the eligibility date ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Have the government sponsor register the [CAC](#term:common-access-card) request and collect fingerprints as early as the rule allows [138](#cite:138).
Submit the reciprocity request on acceptance; escalate at five business days [122](#cite:122).
Verify the foundational cyber certification before the start, since contracted staff need it on commencement [139](#cite:139).
Name the owner and the date for each remaining step and share the list with the hire [144](#cite:144).

name: Sequence the start-date checks in the order the law sets
what: Order the checks by their legal trigger. After the conditional offer: criminal-history questions where the [Fair Chance Act](#term:fair-chance-act) applies [48](#cite:48) and any medical examination [34](#cite:34). Before ordering a [background report](#term:consumer-report): the stand-alone [FCRA disclosure](#term:fair-credit-reporting-act) and written permission; before acting on it: the [pre-adverse-action notice](#term:adverse-action-notice) with the report and the rights summary [136](#cite:136). For a position that works with export-controlled items: the export assessment, apart from the [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) and only for those positions, with no statement that the law requires a citizenship [131](#cite:131). On or by the first day: Section 1 of the I-9; within three business days: Section 2, with the employee choosing the documents [130](#cite:130); within three business days of hire: [E-Verify](#term:e-verify) [128](#cite:128). On commencement: the cyber qualification [139](#cite:139).

evidence.effect: the statutory triggers and windows [128](#cite:128) [130](#cite:130) [131](#cite:131) [136](#cite:136) [48](#cite:48) [34](#cite:34)
evidence.population: federal contractors hiring in the United States

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot compress the windows or waive a step; a check that fails ends the hire whatever its timing ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The DFARS [drug-testing](#term:drug-free-workplace) clause is reserved [134](#cite:134), so testing is a firm policy question, not a federal requirement, outside the FAR's policy program [135](#cite:135).
costs: Paperwork within the first three days; a background-check vendor; a process owner (synthesis).
how_to: Write the sequence into the [offer-to-start](#term:offer-to-start-interval) checklist with the trigger for each step [136](#cite:136) [130](#cite:130) [128](#cite:128).
Keep the export assessment on a separate form from the I-9 and run it only for controlled positions [131](#cite:131).
Enroll in E-Verify within thirty days of award so the three-day window can be met on the first hire [128](#cite:128).

name: A structured onboarding with an insider beside the newcomer
what: The first week, month and quarter are written down, an experienced insider is assigned as guide, what the hire already brings is affirmed, and supervisor contact is kept from falling off. [Institutionalized tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) correlate .24 to .40 with adjustment and social tactics .29 to .47 [152](#cite:152); serial (insider role model) and investiture tactics each roughly halved the odds of leaving within a year at one firm [155](#cite:155); early supervisor and coworker support predicted integration and commitment at ninety days while support itself declined week by week [156](#cite:156). Pre-start contact and a first-day plan also lower the odds that an accepted hire never arrives [144](#cite:144).

evidence.effect: institutionalized tactics r .24–.40, social tactics .29–.47 with adjustment; social acceptance → performance .35, turnover −.12 [152](#cite:152); serial OR 0.44, investiture OR 0.52 for turnover [155](#cite:155)
evidence.population: 183 samples of newcomers [152](#cite:152); 222 newcomers at one financial-services firm [155](#cite:155); 264 university hires over 14 weeks [156](#cite:156)

what_it_does_not_do: The link from adjustment to actual turnover is small [152](#cite:152); [onboarding](#term:onboarding) does not make an unqualified hire qualified or shorten a labor-category [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) [99](#cite:99); the social tactics cost senior time (c-mentoring-capacity-is-senior-billable-time). No causal trial exists [154](#cite:154).
costs: Senior and supervisor hours in the first ninety days; the program document ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Name the insider and the supervisor check-ins before the start; send the first-day plan [144](#cite:144) [152](#cite:152).
Use serial and investiture tactics: an experienced guide, and a message that the hire was chosen for what they are [155](#cite:155).
Hold supervisor contact steady through week fourteen; it falls off otherwise [156](#cite:156).
Invite the [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment)'s own information and feedback seeking; it predicts adjustment on its own [152](#cite:152).

name: A bounded readiness plan with measurable milestones
what: For a hire with strong fundamentals and thin domain experience, write the learning plan with dated milestones that describe what the person can do and bill at each, and measure the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) against them. Output rose 53 percent in the first year where it could be counted, with the fastest learners the ones who stayed [157](#cite:157); [task mastery](#term:newcomer-adjustment) correlates .38 with performance [152](#cite:152); a realistic preview of the work lowers turnover through perceived honesty [13](#cite:13).

evidence.effect: output +53% after one year, pay flatter than output [157](#cite:157); task mastery → performance .38 [152](#cite:152)
evidence.population: windshield installers at one company [157](#cite:157); 183 newcomer samples [152](#cite:152)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not change the [labor category](#term:labor-category) the person can be billed in [99](#cite:99) or guarantee the customer accepts the person at the end (c-customer-rejects-junior-staff); no study of milestone plans themselves was found.
costs: A plan to write and a measure to keep; the ramp is paid at the lower category or from [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: State the category the hire bills in now and the one the plan targets, with the qualification line for each [99](#cite:99).
Set milestones as demonstrable tasks from the firm's own work, not course completions [162](#cite:162).
Review inside the first 14 weeks, while support is still high and before the 90-day outcomes are set [156](#cite:156).

name: A defined junior work package billed at its own category
what: Where the customer will not accept a junior in a senior slot, propose a junior category with a supervised work package and a staffing mix that bills each person at the category they meet. The rule pays only qualified hours [99](#cite:99) and the audit record shows the cost of ignoring it: 101 of 112 unqualified employees improperly charged and tens of millions in recovery [173](#cite:173). A cyber role still needs its certificate on day one [139](#cite:139).

evidence.effect: labor-category qualification rule [99](#cite:99); improper-payment findings [173](#cite:173)

what_it_does_not_do: It may require a task, labor-category or pricing change the customer must approve ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); it does not create a junior category where the contract has none [98](#cite:98).
costs: Lower billing for the junior slot; supervision hours from the senior [99](#cite:99) (synthesis).
how_to: Read the labor-category descriptions and bill each person at the one they meet [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99).
Ask the contracting officer for a substitution or a mix change in writing before the work [99](#cite:99).

name: Pay for training on terms the law still allows, and expect the return in who applies
what: The training is offered openly in the posting and paid for under a written [section 127 plan](#term:section-127-plan) up to \$5,250 a year tax-free [174](#cite:174); where a repayment term is used at all, it takes the shape the strictest states permit: a separate agreement for a transferable credential, at the firm's actual cost, prorated, without interest, never for required training, and never enforced on a termination without misconduct [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168). The retention effect of paying for education came mostly (80 percent) through who chose to join [160](#cite:160); repayment contracts cut quitting by about 15 percent in the research the CFPB cites [166](#cite:166).

evidence.effect: 80% of the retention effect through sorting [160](#cite:160); training contracts ≈ 15% less quitting (cited) [166](#cite:166)

what_it_does_not_do: A repayment term is itself an exposure in California after January 1, 2026 and in Colorado [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168), the NLRB and FTC positions are withdrawn but the CFPB's is not [168](#cite:168) [166](#cite:166), and the training still raises the worker's outside value [161](#cite:161). Pay progression does the rest (sweep 6).
costs: The training; the plan document; counsel for the agreement; the \$5,250 cap on the tax-free part [174](#cite:174) [175](#cite:175).
how_to: Adopt the written plan and tell employees it exists [174](#cite:174).
Say in the posting what the firm pays for; the sorting effect needs applicants to know [160](#cite:160).
If a repayment term is used: separate contract, transferable credential, at cost, prorated, no interest, nothing on termination without misconduct [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168).

name: Allocate mentoring hours and limit concurrent trainees
what: The [mentoring](#term:mentoring) hours are in the plan and in the rates: the senior is named, the hours are budgeted as job-related training cost [175](#cite:175), the number of trainees one senior carries is capped, and the time is treated as the compensation it is, since learning from knowledgeable coworkers is worth four to nine percent of pay [158](#cite:158). The insider beside the [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment) is the strongest [onboarding](#term:onboarding) tactic [152](#cite:152).

evidence.effect: learning 4–9% of total compensation [158](#cite:158); social tactics r .29–.47 [152](#cite:152)

what_it_does_not_do: The protégé''s measurable career gains from mentoring are small [164](#cite:164) [165](#cite:165); the hours come out of billable time or into the [indirect rates](#term:overhead-rate) [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148). No study of trainee caps was found.
costs: Senior hours; higher indirect rates or lower utilisation [148](#cite:148) [99](#cite:99).
how_to: Budget the hours in the indirect rates as training cost before the hire, not after [175](#cite:175) [148](#cite:148).
Name one senior per trainee and cap the load ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
Where the statement of work can carry a mentoring task, put it there so the hours bill [99](#cite:99) (synthesis).

name: Train on representative tasks with the supervisor expecting the skill
what: Training is built from sanitized tasks that look like the work, uses behavioural modelling and error management, has the supervisor state what will change, and schedules the first real use soon after the course. Those are the conditions the transfer literature supports: realistic environments, supervisor support (ρ .31), [transfer climate](#term:transfer-of-training) (.37) and opportunity to perform [162](#cite:162); motivation and self-efficacy matter most for open skills [163](#cite:163).

evidence.effect: supervisor support ρ .31 (peers .14); transfer climate .37; motivation to transfer .43 [162](#cite:162)

what_it_does_not_do: On classified programs the real material may be unavailable and a sanitized task is the ceiling ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the coefficients are carried from a review and the [meta-analyses](#term:meta-analysis) are todos [162](#cite:162).
costs: Someone senior has to build the tasks; supervisor time after the course [162](#cite:162) (synthesis).
how_to: Write the task from the firm's own work; strip what cannot be shared (synthesis).
Have the supervisor tell the trainee what they expect to see used and when [162](#cite:162).
Put the first use within weeks of the course [162](#cite:162).

name: Register an apprenticeship for a technical occupation
what: A [Registered Apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) pairs paid work with related instruction and [mentoring](#term:mentoring) under standards registered with the Department of Labor or a state agency; computer occupations are the third-largest group at 7 percent of about 940,000 participants, growth outside construction was 42 percent over four years, and a program can be approved for GI Bill benefits [172](#cite:172) [177](#cite:177). Completers' career earnings gains were \$240,037 in the federal cost-benefit study [171](#cite:171).

evidence.effect: completers' earnings gains \$240,037; social benefits exceed costs by more than \$49,000 [171](#cite:171)
evidence.population: ten states' Registered Apprenticeship participants [171](#cite:171); FY2024 program data [172](#cite:172)

what_it_does_not_do: The employer's own return has not been measured [171](#cite:171); smaller employers find registration and reporting hard and cost a barrier, and 42 percent of participants complete within a year of the expected date [172](#cite:172). The mentoring component draws on the senior time the firm is short of (c-mentoring-capacity-is-senior-billable-time).
costs: Registration and reporting; apprentice wages (median starting wage \$19 an hour in FY2024); instruction; mentoring [172](#cite:172).
how_to: Use the standards builder and the partner finder; an intermediary can carry the registration [177](#cite:177).
Apply for GI Bill approval through the State Approving Agency where veterans are the pipeline [177](#cite:177).

name: Tie each developmental hire to a named contract or forecast slot
what: Before a developmental hire is made, name the contract, the [labor category](#term:labor-category) and the date the person is meant to fill, and confirm the obligations any pipeline program imposes. Training for non-employees is [unallowable](#term:allowable-cost) [175](#cite:175), a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) cannot be requested ahead of a need [119](#cite:119), a [SkillBridge](#term:skillbridge) partner owes offers to 75 percent of completers [74](#cite:74), and an [apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) carries registration and reporting [172](#cite:172). Whether the demand is real is adjudicated at the plan stage (sweep 7).

evidence.effect: the cost, clearance and program rules that bound speculative development [175](#cite:175) [119](#cite:119) [74](#cite:74)

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot make a forecast true; it limits exposure at the cost of pipeline depth ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). No study of the practice was found.
costs: Slower pipeline growth; [forecasting](#term:demand-forecast) effort (synthesis).
how_to: Write the target slot, category and date into the development plan [175](#cite:175) (synthesis).
Check the program's offer and reporting obligations against the pipeline [74](#cite:74) [172](#cite:172).

name: Track each development cohort's cost, billed service and retention
what: Development is measured the way the economics does: cost against output over tenure. The industry evidence puts the productivity gain from training at about twice the wage gain [159](#cite:159); the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) evidence shows output rising far faster than pay in the first eighteen months [157](#cite:157); the [apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) study shows the method applied to participants and society but not to employers [171](#cite:171); the tuition evidence shows most of the retention return arrives through sorting [160](#cite:160). A cohort record of training cost, [mentoring](#term:mentoring) hours, billed hours by category and retention at 12 and 24 months is the firm's own version ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

evidence.effect: output +0.6% vs wages +0.3% per training point [159](#cite:159); output +53% in year one with pay flatter [157](#cite:157)

what_it_does_not_do: It takes two years to say anything, and some individual investments will fail whatever the cohort returns (synthesis); the measured returns in the evidence are industry- or firm-level averages [159](#cite:159) [157](#cite:157), not predictions for one hire, and no employer-side apprenticeship return was found [171](#cite:171).
costs: [Record-keeping](#term:applicant-record-retention) by cohort; a two-year horizon (synthesis).
how_to: Record per trainee: training cost, mentoring hours, billed hours by category, pay, and status at 12 and 24 months (synthesis).
Compare cohort billed value against cohort cost; judge the program, not the last departure [159](#cite:159) [171](#cite:171).

name: Review pay at capability milestones against the market and the peers
what: Each person's pay is reviewed when their capability changes, against the [OEWS](#term:oews) and cleared-market figures and against the peers doing [substantially equal work](#term:equal-pay-act), and raises are kept similar across peers unless the difference can be explained. Quits respond to own pay mostly through comparison with higher-paid peers and are insensitive when raises are similar [182](#cite:182); below-median earners who learn peer pay search for other jobs [92](#cite:92); the Equal Pay Act requires curing a gap upward [112](#cite:112). Where the rate cannot carry the review, the rate-relief request is the next [lever](#term:lever-record) (l-rate-relief-request).

evidence.effect: peer-comparison driven quits; separations insensitive to similar raises [182](#cite:182); pay ρ −.17 [178](#cite:178)
evidence.population: employees of a large U.S. retailer [182](#cite:182); 316 turnover studies [178](#cite:178)

what_it_does_not_do: Pay is a modest predictor on its own (−.17) and cannot buy back commitment, fit or a bad supervisor [178](#cite:178); the rate ceiling may leave no room [98](#cite:98); a raise above peers for one person is the comparison that moves the others [182](#cite:182).
costs: Recurring payroll; a rate discussion with the customer where the ceiling binds [98](#cite:98) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Tie the review to the readiness milestones and the [labor-category qualification](#term:labor-category-qualifications) lines [99](#cite:99) (synthesis).
Compare within the firm first, then to OEWS and the [cleared](#term:security-clearance) survey [92](#cite:92) [110](#cite:110) [89](#cite:89).
Keep raises similar across peers in substantially equal work; explain any difference [182](#cite:182) [112](#cite:112).

name: A technical ladder and lateral moves in place of the one promotion
what: Offer growth that is not the management title: a technical ladder with scope and pay steps, cross-program moves, and a promotion into management decided on managerial potential and teamwork experience rather than on individual output. Internal mobility is among the practices most strongly tied to lower [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) (ρ −.25) [181](#cite:181); promoting the top seller costs 7.5 percent of manager value added per doubling of prior sales and workers with more teamwork experience make better managers without being promoted more [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185). Each move leaves a vacancy with the full clock behind it (c-internal-move-opens-another-vacancy).

evidence.effect: internal mobility ρ −.25 with unit turnover [181](#cite:181); −7.5% manager value added per doubling of prior sales [185](#cite:185)
evidence.population: 82 unit-level studies [181](#cite:181); sales workers at 131–214 firms [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185)

what_it_does_not_do: A title does not substitute for pay that has lagged [178](#cite:178) or for work the person finds stagnant ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); a small firm's ladder has few rungs and the lateral move needs another program to go to (sweep 7, H1).
costs: Pay steps on the ladder; the backfill behind every move [126](#cite:126) (synthesis).
how_to: Write the technical ladder with scope and pay at each step; separate it from the management path (synthesis).
Decide management promotions on evidence of managerial potential and teamwork, not individual output [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185).
Start the backfill before the move and clear named-personnel moves with the customer [188](#cite:188) [126](#cite:126).

name: Regular check-ins by the firm's own manager, with the work on the table
what: A manager of the firm's own stays in regular contact with each person at a customer site, talking about the work, the supervision, the tools and the fit, and listening for the two strongest signals, wanting to leave and looking [178](#cite:178). Leadership quality predicts quitting at ρ −.24, commitment at −.29 and satisfaction at −.28 [178](#cite:178); unit engagement relates to turnover across 7,939 business units [183](#cite:183); an undermining supervisor tripled a [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment)'s hazard of leaving [156](#cite:156).

evidence.effect: leadership ρ −.24; commitment −.29; satisfaction −.28; withdrawal cognitions .56 [178](#cite:178)
evidence.population: 316 turnover studies [178](#cite:178); 7,939 business units in 36 companies [183](#cite:183)

what_it_does_not_do: Stay interviews and recognition programs as such have no evidence base found; the check-in works through the relationship the leadership and engagement [correlations](#term:correlation-coefficient) describe [178](#cite:178) [183](#cite:183), and the correlations are not causal estimates of any conversation practice. An undermining supervisor is a hazard the check-in cannot offset [156](#cite:156).
costs: Management time; the meetings the row warns against if they bring the employee nothing ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Schedule the check-in; ask about workload strain, role conflict and fit, the predictors that matter [178](#cite:178).
Act on what is heard with the customer where the work is the problem (synthesis).
Treat voiced job search as the signal it is, at ρ .40 [178](#cite:178).
