name: Show the capacity risk of a vacancy and negotiate scope or temporary support
what: When a vacancy opens, put the capacity gap in front of the customer with its date and ask for a priority call, reduced scope or temporary support rather than covering it silently with the remaining staff. The strain of covering predicts quitting (stress ρ .21; role conflict .15; work–life conflict .19) where hours as such do not (−.10) [178](#cite:178); a named key person's departure already requires notice and a substitute [188](#cite:188); unbilled hours are the customer's problem too [99](#cite:99) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

evidence.effect: stress .21; role conflict .15; work–life conflict .19; workload −.10 [178](#cite:178)

what_it_does_not_do: The customer may decline to reduce scope; the cover then continues with the strain it brings (synthesis), and strain, not hours, is what predicts quitting [178](#cite:178). No study of capacity negotiation with a customer was found; the [lever](#term:lever-record) rests on the contract's key-personnel and notice mechanics [188](#cite:188).
costs: A harder conversation with the customer; possible reduced billing (synthesis).
how_to: State the vacancy's hours, the backfill clock and the tasks that will slip [126](#cite:126) (synthesis).
Ask for a priority order or a temporary substitute before the cover becomes the plan [188](#cite:188).

name: Seek the customer's approval for the flexibility the work allows, and state the limits truthfully
what: Where the contract and the classification allow it, obtain written customer approval for schedule flexibility or partial remote work, and where they do not, say so accurately in the posting and the offer. Workers price a work-from-home option at about 8 percent of pay and a predictable schedule at about 20 percent [115](#cite:115); long commutes raise transfer probability [194](#cite:194); a truthful account of the conditions is the mechanism by which previews lower turnover [13](#cite:13).

evidence.effect: WFH ≈ 8% of wages; schedule predictability ≈ 20% [115](#cite:115); commute 45+ minutes +10 points transfer [194](#cite:194)
evidence.population: call-centre applicants [115](#cite:115); teachers in one district [194](#cite:194)

what_it_does_not_do: Classified work cannot leave the facility [119](#cite:119) and the customer's hours are the customer's; the [lever](#term:lever-record) changes what is asked for and what is promised, not the contract ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: A request the customer may refuse; a narrower pool where the answer is no [115](#cite:115) (synthesis).
how_to: Read the contract and the DD 254 for what may be done off-site; ask the contracting officer in writing (synthesis).
Put the real schedule and site in the posting and the preview [13](#cite:13).

name: Tell people what is known about the contract's future, and what is not
what: Communicate the option years, [recompetes](#term:recompete), protests and pipeline as facts with dates, name the redeployment options that exist, and say plainly what the firm cannot promise. Honesty is the mechanism by which realistic previews lower voluntary turnover [13](#cite:13); wanting to leave and perceived alternatives are the strongest predictors of leaving [178](#cite:178); no federal [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) with a [successor contractor](#term:successor-contractor) exists any longer [186](#cite:186).

evidence.effect: perceived organizational honesty mediates RJP → lower turnover [13](#cite:13); withdrawal cognitions .56, alternatives .23 [178](#cite:178)

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot make an unfunded contract real or promise an assignment the firm does not control ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the demand side is sweep 7.
costs: Candour about uncertainty; some people will act on it (synthesis).
how_to: Share the contract calendar and the pipeline status on a fixed rhythm (synthesis).
Name the redeployment options and their conditions; do not imply a right of first refusal [186](#cite:186).

name: Build the links, fit and sacrifice that make leaving costly
what: [Embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness), the web of links, fit and things a person would give up by leaving, predicts quitting at ρ −.26 [178](#cite:178) and on-the-job embeddedness more than off-the-job [192](#cite:192); it is the mechanism through which [onboarding tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) kept people at one firm (OR 0.42) [155](#cite:155); [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) is the practice most strongly tied to a unit staying together (−.40) [181](#cite:181). For a person at a customer site the firm's links have to be built on purpose ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

evidence.effect: job embeddedness ρ −.26 [178](#cite:178); on-the-job embeddedness OR 0.42 for turnover [155](#cite:155); firm-specific training −.40 [181](#cite:181)

what_it_does_not_do: The practices suggested to build embeddedness (teams, gatherings, fit, flexible scheduling) are untested [192](#cite:192); the off-the-job half is the community''s, not the firm''s [192](#cite:192).
costs: Firm-specific training and the time of the people who provide the links [181](#cite:181) (synthesis).
how_to: Give each off-site person a firm-side team, a [mentor](#term:mentoring) and a role in something the firm owns (synthesis).
Invest in firm-specific skills and tools, the training that keeps units together [181](#cite:181).

name: Cross-train the key tasks, document the handoffs and name the successor
what: For every contract task and customer relationship held by one person, train a second, write the handoff down and name a successor who meets the [labor category](#term:labor-category). [Replacement costs](#term:replacement-cost) are largest for specialised skills in thin markets [193](#cite:193); [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) is the practice most strongly tied to lower [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) (−.40) [181](#cite:181); a named key person's substitute must meet or exceed the requirement [188](#cite:188); succession metrics are part of the human-capital reporting standard [46](#cite:46).

evidence.effect: replacement costs larger for specialised skills and thin markets [193](#cite:193); firm-specific training −.40 [181](#cite:181)
evidence.population: 34,000 worker deaths in German records [193](#cite:193); 82 unit-level studies [181](#cite:181)

what_it_does_not_do: It spends current delivery time (the row's trade-off) and the senior hours the firm is short of (c-mentoring-capacity-is-senior-billable-time); the evidence is a unit-level [correlation](#term:correlation-coefficient) between firm-specific training and lower turnover [181](#cite:181), not a study of handoff documentation, and the replacement-cost case rests on administrative records of unexpected deaths [193](#cite:193).
costs: Senior and second-person hours; [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) in the rates [148](#cite:148) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: List the single-holder tasks and relationships; pair each with a trainee and a date (synthesis).
Keep the successor's résumé against the labor-category line so the substitute is ready [188](#cite:188) [99](#cite:99).

name: A written departure protocol for named and cleared staff
what: A written account of what happens on the day a person gives notice: the contracting officer's notice and substitute request within the clause's period [188](#cite:188); the termination report and the removal from access for a [cleared](#term:security-clearance) employee [189](#cite:189) [119](#cite:119); the agency notification where the person is named in a pending proposal [108](#cite:108); the handoff and the successor (l-cross-training-and-documented-handoffs); the [WARN](#term:warn-act) check where the firm has 100 or more employees [191](#cite:191); and the exit conversation that records why, for the cohort measure (l-cohort-return-tracking) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

evidence.effect: the clause, reporting and notification duties a departure triggers [188](#cite:188) [189](#cite:189) [108](#cite:108)
evidence.population: federal contractors with named or cleared staff

what_it_does_not_do: It does not keep the person or shorten the backfill clock [126](#cite:126); exit interviews have no evidence found as a retention instrument (synthesis).
costs: Security-officer and contracts time on the day; a document kept current (synthesis).
how_to: Notify the contracting officer and propose the substitute inside the clause's period [188](#cite:188).
Report the termination and remove access; keep the adverse-information duty in mind afterwards [189](#cite:189).
Tell the agency if the person is named in a live proposal [108](#cite:108).

name: Non-solicitation only where it is collateral to a real collaboration
what: In [teaming](#term:teaming-agreement) and [subcontract](#term:subcontractor) agreements, use no agreement with the [prime](#term:prime-contractor) or a teammate not to hire each other's people; a [no-poach agreement](#term:no-poach-agreement) is illegal without any showing of harm and may be prosecuted criminally, while a [non-solicitation term](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) subordinate and collateral to a legitimate collaboration and reasonably necessary to it is judged on its effects [187](#cite:187). [Noncompetes](#term:noncompete-agreement) on the person are a state-law question after the federal rule's vacatur [169](#cite:169) and repayment terms are narrowed by state statute [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168).

evidence.effect: no-poach agreements illegal and criminally prosecutable; ancillary non-solicit terms judged on effects [187](#cite:187)

what_it_does_not_do: It does not stop the prime from hiring the firm's people on their own initiative; the hold has to be in the job (l-embeddedness-building), and the guidelines treat an agreement between competing employers not to hire each other's people as a criminal matter whatever its label [187](#cite:187).
costs: Counsel's review of every teaming agreement ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Strike bare no-hire terms; keep any non-solicit scoped to the collaboration and its duration [187](#cite:187).
Do not exchange compensation information with the prime or a competitor [187](#cite:187).

name: Confirm funding, authority, start date and intent before recruiting spend
what: Before a posting goes out, write down the contract or task order, the [labor category](#term:labor-category), the funding line, the person who can say yes, and the start date, and classify the opening as funded, proposed or speculative. A [clearance](#term:security-clearance) cannot be requested ahead of a contract need [119](#cite:119); a proposed key person must be reported if unavailable [108](#cite:108) and may not be named without a reasonable basis to deliver them [203](#cite:203); a pre-employment investigation needs a written commitment and a start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119); recruiting spend before funding is [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) [148](#cite:148).

evidence.effect: the sponsorship, proposal-representation and start-date rules [119](#cite:119) [108](#cite:108) [203](#cite:203)

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot make a proposal win or a task order arrive; it delays sourcing for work that later becomes real (the row's trade-off), and a clearance cannot be requested ahead of the need in any case [119](#cite:119). No study of [requisition](#term:requisition) confirmation practices was found; the [lever](#term:lever-record) rests on the rules [119](#cite:119) [203](#cite:203).
costs: A conversation with the customer before the posting; slower starts on speculative openings ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Name the contract, category, funding line, decision authority and start date on the requisition (synthesis).
For proposal openings, use the contingent-offer protocol and keep the commitment current [203](#cite:203) [108](#cite:108).

name: A short scorecard agreed with the customer, with every requirement traced to its source
what: The [requisition](#term:requisition) is written as a scorecard of a few deliverables and the competencies that produce them, each requirement labelled as contractual (the [labor category](#term:labor-category)), customer-required in writing, or preferred, with the approval authority named and an example profile reviewed with the customer before posting; scope, pay and urgency are reconfirmed whenever a requirement changes. The category line is the enforceable definition [99](#cite:99) and is what the audit checked [173](#cite:173); a requirement with [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact) must be job-related [30](#cite:30) [32](#cite:32); structured, scored criteria predict performance where judgement does not [1](#cite:1) [7](#cite:7); the title and pay set who applies [65](#cite:65); the customer specifies the result, not the hire [197](#cite:197).

evidence.effect: structured interviews .42, work samples .33 vs unstructured .19 [1](#cite:1); mechanical combination .44 vs .28 [7](#cite:7)

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot make the customer explain a rejection; no study of rejection feedback or of shared scorecards with customers was found ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Restarting after a requirement change still loses engaged candidates [16](#cite:16).
costs: Upfront coordination time with the customer; a posting delayed until the scorecard is agreed (synthesis).
how_to: List deliverables, then the few competencies that produce them; drop the rest to preferred [32](#cite:32) (synthesis).
Trace each requirement to the category, a written customer requirement or a preference; name who can waive it [99](#cite:99) [197](#cite:197).
Review one example profile with the customer against the scorecard before posting (synthesis).
When a requirement changes, reconfirm scope, pay range and urgency before continuing [16](#cite:16) [15](#cite:15).

name: Review milestones and escalation contacts agreed with the customer
what: Where the customer approves named staff, agree the review steps, the days each takes and the escalation contact before the first résumé is sent, and tell the candidate the calendar. The clause carried gives the contractor 30 days to propose a substitute and the government no period to answer [188](#cite:188); candidates accept earlier offers more often [15](#cite:15) and withdraw from processes they perceive badly [16](#cite:16); the customer may specify and reject but may not run the hire [197](#cite:197).

evidence.effect: earlier offers accepted more often, no later penalty [15](#cite:15); withdrawal tied to process perceptions [16](#cite:16)
evidence.population: applicants in the speed and withdrawal studies [15](#cite:15) [16](#cite:16)

what_it_does_not_do: It cannot compel the customer's decision; the firm controls the asking and the telling, not the answer ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). No study of customer approval cycles was found (the [ledger](#term:hypothesis-ledger) closes E5 as unstudied); the delay evidence is about the firm's own process, where earlier offers are accepted more often [15](#cite:15).
costs: A negotiation with the customer's contracting and program staff (synthesis).
how_to: Put the review steps and days in the contract's staffing plan or a written agreement (synthesis).
Give the candidate the calendar and a named contact; update them when a step slips [144](#cite:144).

name: An all-in acquisition budget per role, set against the vacancy's cost
what: A budget per [requisition](#term:requisition) that covers agency fees, boards, [referral](#term:referral-hiring) payments, travel, relocation, recruiter time and any [sign-on bonus](#term:signing-bonus), set against what the [vacancy costs](#term:vacancy-cost) in contribution and delivery. The 2025 medians were \$1,200 per nonexecutive hire and \$10,625 per executive hire, with those components in the definition [196](#cite:196); sign-on bonuses are used by 80 percent of organisations and evaluated by 12 percent [118](#cite:118), and on cost-type work are [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) only under an established plan [100](#cite:100); the replacement-cost median is about a fifth of salary [180](#cite:180).

evidence.effect: median cost-per-hire \$1,200 / \$10,625 (2025) [196](#cite:196); replacement cost ≈ 21% of salary [180](#cite:180)

what_it_does_not_do: Fees buy access, not acceptance or retention (the row's trade-off); no primary on [fee](#term:fee) levels was found and no study of sign-on bonus effectiveness exists [118](#cite:118); a tight budget prolongs the vacancy it was meant to price ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: The budget itself; the analysis to set it (synthesis).
how_to: Price the vacancy first: unbilled hours, the unit-level effects, the replacement-cost share [99](#cite:99) [181](#cite:181) [180](#cite:180).
Reserve search firms for the roles where the vacancy cost exceeds the fee (synthesis).
Put bonuses under a written plan before the work [100](#cite:100).

name: Cap the payroll carried ahead of funded work
what: A limit on the number of people and the months of payroll the firm will carry before the first invoice on the work they were hired for, with developmental and [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) hires staged against that cap. A [proper invoice](#term:prompt-payment) is paid in 30 days by default [202](#cite:202) and with a [15-day goal](#term:accelerated-payment) for small business contractors [201](#cite:201); payroll before billing is [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) in the pools [148](#cite:148); a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) cannot be requested ahead of the need in any case [119](#cite:119).

evidence.effect: the 30-day default and 15-day goal for payment [202](#cite:202) [201](#cite:201); indirect-cost treatment of unbilled payroll [148](#cite:148)

what_it_does_not_do: A low cap slows the response when work arrives (the row's trade-off); it does not shorten the [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) or make a clearance requestable before the need [119](#cite:119), and the payment clock it is set against is a default, not a guarantee [202](#cite:202).
costs: Opportunities declined or delayed when the cap is reached ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: State the cap in people and months; count every hire made before its first billable hour against it (synthesis).
Invoice promptly and ask for the accelerated-payment goal where it applies [201](#cite:201) [202](#cite:202).

name: Estimate what each vacancy costs and rank the openings by it
what: For each open [requisition](#term:requisition), estimate the unbilled hours, the delivery at risk, the strain on the people covering it, and the [replacement cost](#term:replacement-cost), and rank the openings by that estimate and by feasibility rather than treating them alike. Replacement cost runs about a fifth of salary in the case-study median and far more for the highly paid [180](#cite:180); [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) lowers customer satisfaction and productivity at about −.22 [181](#cite:181); covering a vacancy shows in stress and role conflict [178](#cite:178); unbilled hours are the contract's missing revenue [99](#cite:99).

evidence.effect: replacement cost ≈ 21% of salary [180](#cite:180); unit turnover −.22 with customer satisfaction and productivity [181](#cite:181)

what_it_does_not_do: Estimates need assumptions and unbilled revenue is not lost profit (the row's trade-off); ranking means some openings get less attention. The measured figures are a case-study median [180](#cite:180) and unit-level [correlations](#term:correlation-coefficient) [181](#cite:181), not the firm's own numbers, and the larger multiples in circulation rest on no named study [195](#cite:195).
costs: Analysis time; an uncomfortable ranking ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: For each opening: unbilled hours per month, tasks at risk, who is covering and for how long, replacement-cost share [99](#cite:99) [180](#cite:180) [178](#cite:178).
Rank by cost and feasibility; give the top of the list the owner and the budget (synthesis).

name: Check that the market salary, loaded, fits under the category ceiling before posting
what: Take the market pay for the category from [OEWS](#term:oews) and the [cleared](#term:security-clearance) survey [110](#cite:110) [89](#cite:89), apply the firm's fringe, [overhead](#term:overhead-rate), [G&A](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) and profit layers in the order a government cost proposal assumes [206](#cite:206), and compare the result with the labor-category rate or the schedule ceiling [98](#cite:98) [111](#cite:111). Where it does not fit, decide before posting whether the work can be redistributed, delivered as a team at mixed categories, or priced again through the contract's adjustment clause [117](#cite:117); the market moves about 3 percent a year while the rate waits [103](#cite:103).

evidence.effect: the rate build-up [206](#cite:206) and the ceiling and adjustment rules [98](#cite:98) [111](#cite:111) [117](#cite:117)
evidence.population: contractors pricing labor under T&M, labor-hour and schedule contracts

what_it_does_not_do: It does not change the rate; existing contract terms may bar the preferred change (the row's trade-off); the test is [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from the [rate build-up](#term:wrap-rate) [206](#cite:206) and the category rule [98](#cite:98), and no source states it as such.
costs: A rate calculation per [requisition](#term:requisition); a hard conversation where the answer is no (synthesis).
how_to: Market salary × (1 + fringe) × (1 + overhead) × (1 + G&A) × (1 + profit) against the ceiling rate [206](#cite:206) (synthesis).
Where it fails, redistribute, re-team, or request adjustment inside the clause's window [117](#cite:117).

name: A rolling forecast of openings by category, with the pipelines it implies
what: A dated list of expected openings by [labor category](#term:labor-category), contract and probability, with the pipelines for recurring skills maintained before the vacancies open. The planning principles ask for the critical skills, the gaps, the capability and the measure [205](#cite:205); the clocks the forecast buys time against are the 45-day median fill [43](#cite:43) and the 197-to-243-day [clearance](#term:security-clearance) [126](#cite:126); the signals are the firm's own pipeline and the public series on openings and shortages [57](#cite:57) [71](#cite:71).

evidence.effect: the five planning principles [205](#cite:205); the clocks a forecast runs ahead of [43](#cite:43) [126](#cite:126)
evidence.population: federal agencies (the principles); small firms (the clocks)

what_it_does_not_do: Forecasts can be wrong and pipelines cost effort without an opening (the row's trade-off); no study of forecast accuracy at small contractors was found, and a cache of cleared people cannot be built in any case [119](#cite:119).
costs: Planning time; relationships maintained without an opening; a forecast revised each quarter ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: List expected openings with category, contract, date and probability; revise quarterly [205](#cite:205) (synthesis).
Keep the [referral](#term:referral-hiring) network, the university and military pipelines and the already-eligible contacts warm for recurring categories [60](#cite:60) [74](#cite:74).

name: Customer-consented partner support for specific gaps, inside the subcontracting limits
what: A gap the firm cannot staff is filled with a teammate's or [subcontractor](#term:subcontractor)'s people, with the contracting officer's [advance consent](#term:consent-to-subcontract) where the clause requires it [199](#cite:199), inside the limit of half the amount paid on a [set-aside](#term:set-aside) services contract for partners that are not [similarly situated](#term:limitations-on-subcontracting) [198](#cite:198), at the subcontractor's own category rates [98](#cite:98), and with no agreement not to hire each other's people [187](#cite:187).

evidence.effect: the consent, limitation and antitrust rules [199](#cite:199) [198](#cite:198) [187](#cite:187)
evidence.population: small primes on set-aside and cost-type or T&M contracts

what_it_does_not_do: Lower margin, less control and the customer's approval (the row's trade-off); the partner's people remain the partner's to move ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: The partner's margin; the consent request; the limitation accounting at each period end [198](#cite:198) [199](#cite:199).
how_to: Check the subcontracted share against the limit before adding the partner [198](#cite:198).
Request consent with the subcontractor named and priced [199](#cite:199).
Keep any [non-solicit term](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) collateral to the collaboration [187](#cite:187).

name: A pipeline record of where candidates stop and why, reviewed against the evidence
what: One record per [requisition](#term:requisition) of every candidate, the stage at which they left and the reason, kept with the records the law already requires, application and [selection records](#term:applicant-record-retention) for a year [200](#cite:200), applicant-flow records for the [adverse-impact](#term:adverse-impact) computation [31](#cite:31), and the longer periods the state automated-decision rules set [40](#cite:40); the stage losses and the source performance are reviewed against the evidence rather than the last case. HR practitioners' beliefs diverge from the research most on selection [204](#cite:204); the human-capital standard names the metrics [46](#cite:46).

evidence.effect: research–practice gaps among 959 HR professionals, largest in selection [204](#cite:204)

what_it_does_not_do: Consistent definitions are needed and reporting can become a burden (the row's trade-off); the record describes the firm's own pipeline, not the market ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
costs: A shared record kept current; candidate data handled under the retention and privacy rules [200](#cite:200) [40](#cite:40).
how_to: Record stage, outcome and reason for every candidate; keep what the law requires for as long as it requires [200](#cite:200) [31](#cite:31) [40](#cite:40).
Review stage losses and source yields each quarter against the selection and attraction evidence [204](#cite:204) [1](#cite:1).

name: One accountable owner per requisition, with the calendar
what: One person owns the [requisition](#term:requisition) from opening to first productive day, with the authority to decide and the calendar of every clock on it: the posting, the screen, the interview, the offer, the customer's review, the [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship), the credential and the start. Earlier offers are accepted more often [15](#cite:15), withdrawal follows a badly perceived process [16](#cite:16), and each week between acceptance and start raises the odds the hire never arrives [144](#cite:144).

evidence.effect: speed of offer → acceptance [15](#cite:15); process perceptions → withdrawal [16](#cite:16); interval → no-shows [144](#cite:144)
evidence.population: applicants and new hires in the cited studies

what_it_does_not_do: The owner needs protected time and decision authority (the row's trade-off); no study of requisition ownership itself was found (the [ledger](#term:hypothesis-ledger) closes E1 as unstudied), and the speed evidence the [lever](#term:lever-record) rests on is about offer timing and process perceptions [15](#cite:15) [16](#cite:16), not about who owns the process.
costs: Protected time for the owner; decision authority delegated to them ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to: Name the owner on the requisition; give them the calendar and the authority to decide (synthesis).
Measure the requisition's clocks and report them weekly [15](#cite:15) [144](#cite:144) (synthesis).
